Passages:
[1] [Equity Compensation > About Your Ownership in GitLab > Questions about your stock plan or retail account > Exercise Window After Termination]
If your employment ends for whatever reason, you have a three month window to exercise your vested options, or lose them. During this window you would have to pay the exercise price and in some cases the tax on the gain in value of your stock options, which could be considerable.

[2] [Equity Compensation > About Your Ownership in GitLab > Exercising Your Options]
"Exercising your options" means buying the stock per your option agreement. You pay the exercise price that was set when the options were first granted and you receive stock certificates back. To give team members an opportunity to benefit from any existing tax incentives that may be available (including under the US the Dutch tax laws and tax laws of your country of residence) we have made the stock immediately exercisable. This means you can exercise your right to purchase the unvested shares under your option to start your holding period. However, the Company retains a repurchase right for the unvested shares if your employment or other services ends for any reason. An early exercise of unvested stock may have important tax implications and you should consult your tax advisor before making such a decision.

While the company has the right to repurchase the unvested shares upon your termination of services, the company is not obligated to do so. Accordingly you could lose some or all of the investment you made. Because we are a young company there are lots of risks, so be aware and informed of the risks.

[3] [Equity Compensation > About Your Ownership in GitLab > Questions about your stock plan or retail account > Option Expiration]
If you leave GitLab, you will generally be able to exercise your options that are vested (as of the last day of service).
In addition, if not otherwise expired (through termination of your employment), your stock options expire 10 years after they were issued.

Question: In the United Kingdom, if I receive a stock grant after my employment has already ended, will I still be able to exercise my options within the standard 90‑day window?

Answer:
Based on the provided context, the answer is **no** (or rather, the premise of the question is flawed based on the text).

The context states that if your employment ends, you have a three-month window to exercise your **vested options**. It does not mention receiving new stock grants *after* employment has ended. Typically, stock options are granted during employment. If you have already left, you would not receive a new grant to exercise within a post-termination window; rather, you would be exercising options that were **already granted and vested** prior to your departure.

Furthermore, the context does not specify different rules for the United Kingdom regarding the 90-day (three-month) window; it states the rule generally applies if employment ends. However, since you cannot receive a *new* grant after termination to then exercise it within that window, the scenario described in the question does not align with the standard process described in the text.

**Key points from the text:**
1.  You have a **three-month window** to exercise **vested options** after employment ends.
2.  Options are granted and vest during employment.
3.  The text does not support the idea of receiving a *new* grant after termination that is then subject to the 90-day exercise window.

Therefore, you cannot exercise options from a grant received *after* employment ends because such a grant would not typically exist under the described plan. You can only exercise options that were **vested as of your last day of service**.
